title: From carried state to gated word models
question: What must a network carry, protect, reset, and expose to use earlier words?

contribution.text: Copy the previous hidden activation into context so the current representation depends on prior inputs.

beginner.heading: Carry a state, not a word list
beginner.body: Elman's context units copy the previous hidden activation. The copied activation and current input jointly shape the next hidden state, so memory is part of ongoing processing rather than a separate fixed window.

beginner.heading: Predict before revealing the trace
beginner.body: Two histories end on the same abstract token. Decide whether their current states must match, then inspect the copied context and resulting state in the synthetic trace.

beginner.heading: Prediction pressure organizes state
beginner.body: The article trains its networks to predict the next item and inspects how hidden activity reflects lexical and sequential regularities without supplied category labels.

beginner.heading: Carried state is not unlimited memory
beginner.body: Repeated nonlinear updates can decay earlier information, and the displayed outputs are not a normalized next-word distribution. The trace shows history dependence, not long-context language competence.

expert.heading: Separate the fixed copy from the learned transform
expert.body: The one-to-one hidden-to-context links have fixed weight 1.0; context-to-hidden and input-to-hidden paths remain trainable. The atlas teaching recurrence is a reconstruction, not a compact equation printed by Elman.

expert.heading: Audit types, tokens, and averaging
expert.body: Contextual token states can cluster by lexical regularity, but the article also checks the averaging artifact and a novel-word context test. Those inspections do not turn each coordinate into a stable semantic feature.

expert.heading: Keep the output metric unnormalized
expert.body: The word experiment fits successor-likelihood vectors with squared error and reports RMS and cosine evidence. It does not define a vocabulary softmax or sentence likelihood.

expert.heading: Forward recurrence is not full temporal credit
expert.body: The previous activation affects the next forward state, but current-step output error updates the trainable paths locally. Keep that training boundary and the paper's numerical and dynamical memory limits visible.

contribution.text: Protect a unit-weight recurrent cell path and learn separate controls for writing and exposing state.

beginner.heading: A state can survive while its teaching signal fades
beginner.body: An ordinary recurrent path repeatedly scales a backward teaching signal. The protected cell path isolates a unit local factor so the direct cell contribution does not decay or explode at every step.

beginner.heading: Write and expose are different decisions
beginner.body: The input gate controls whether a candidate changes the protected state. The output gate controls whether that state affects the rest of the network.

beginner.heading: The original cell has two gates
beginner.body: This stage has input and output gates, a fixed self-loop, and no learned forget gate or cell-state-to-gate peepholes. Its long-delay evidence comes from synthetic tasks.

expert.heading: Compare repeated temporal factors
expert.body: The paper's analysis writes distant error as a product of local temporal derivatives. The synthetic ledger shows only a scalar path term and never labels it the complete Jacobian or parameter gradient.

expert.heading: Trace the constant-error carousel
expert.body: The source cell uses a linear internal state with a fixed unit self-connection; input and output gate activations scale access around that path. Source symbols and the neutral ledger remain side by side.

expert.heading: Mark every truncation boundary
expert.body: The efficient source algorithm preserves recurrent error inside cells while cutting specified outgoing paths from cells and gates. It is not exact full-gradient backpropagation through the complete network.

expert.heading: Keep mechanism and benchmark scope separate
expert.body: The long-lag experiments are synthetic and retain delayed-XOR, parity, counting, capacity, drift, cost, and parameter-overhead limitations. Later gates cannot be imported to repair those boundaries retroactively.

contribution.text: Replace the fixed state-retention self-weight with a learned forget gate for continual streams.

beginner.heading: A protected accumulator still needs boundaries
beginner.body: On an unsegmented stream, repeated additions can drive the original state away from a useful range. A fixed decay loses arbitrary-delay retention, while a teacher-supplied reset assumes known boundaries.

beginner.heading: Predict retained activation
beginner.body: Keep the previous state and input-gated write fixed while comparing near-retain, gradual-decay, and near-reset. The gate changes activation retention, not the learned weights.

beginner.heading: Read learned reset inside its task
beginner.body: The paper compares external and learned resets on continual embedded Reber grammar and tests a continual noisy temporal-order task. These are synthetic sequence families, not language-model results.

beginner.heading: Do not confuse state reset with parameter forgetting
beginner.body: The mechanism changes carried activation. It does not erase learned weights or establish a result about catastrophic forgetting, natural language, or unknown real-world boundaries.

expert.heading: Replace the unit self-weight
expert.body: Journal equations 6–7 multiply the previous cell state by the block-shared forget-gate activation before adding the input-gated candidate. The crosswalk preserves the source's scalar block notation.

expert.heading: Keep the journal eligibility trace version-bound
expert.body: Positive bias initializes near standard LSTM; the truncated trace carries through the forget gate and resets with state. The February report prints a different derivative term, so the displayed rule stays journal-bound.

expert.heading: Audit both continual protocols
expert.body: Keep the CERG protocol, external-reset comparison, learned self-reset behavior, noncontinual control, and CNTO results tied to their stated topologies, trial counts, and version differences.

expert.heading: Synthetic reset evidence stays synthetic
expert.body: The work provides no released code, learned parameters, uncertainty estimates, optimized topology study, or natural-language evaluation. Peepholes remain absent.

contribution.text: Let input, forget, and output gates inspect protected cell state through weighted peephole links.

beginner.heading: A closed output can hide the timer
beginner.body: Traditional gates can see exposed cell output, but a closed output gate hides the protected internal state. The 2002 extension gives each gate a direct weighted read of that state.

beginner.heading: Inspect, update, then inspect again
beginner.body: Input and forget gates inspect the previous state; the cell updates; then the output gate inspects the new state. A peephole changes what a gate can see, not the meaning of the forget multiplier.

beginner.heading: Timing evidence is narrower than language
beginner.body: The paper studies measuring and generating delays with one-cell synthetic timing tasks, including an ablation after training. Those results do not establish language-model gains.

beginner.heading: Reading a timer does not remove capacity limits
beginner.body: Direct state reads help gates inspect hidden activation. The paper still identifies limits in capacity, gate learning, noisy triggers, and initialization; its results are not word-language-model evidence.

expert.heading: Begin from the forget-gated baseline
expert.body: The 2002 paper explicitly inherits the 2000 forget-gate recurrence. Its new contribution is cell-state-to-gate visibility, not another retention operator.

expert.heading: Preserve equations 19–21 and update order
expert.body: Input and forget gate preactivations include weighted s_c(t−1); output-gate preactivation includes weighted s_c(t). The neutral fixture mirrors only that ordering and labels its numbers synthetic.

expert.heading: Keep truncated learning separate
expert.body: Equations 22–26 add peephole partials and weight updates without propagating gate error back through those links into the constant-error carousel. Three added weights per cell do not mean zero overhead.

expert.heading: Audit timing results and ablations
expert.body: Keep MSD, GTS, PFG, topology, threshold, and post-training-gate-removal evidence distinct. Removing a trained gate is not the same experiment as training without it.

expert.heading: Do not generalize a one-cell timer
expert.body: The source itself retains memory-capacity, solution-complexity, and truncation limits. The synthetic protocols have no ordinary-RNN control or natural-language benchmark.

contribution.text: Combine Elman-style recurrent state with a normalized next-word distribution at speech-recognition scale.

beginner.heading: Replace the explicit window with carried state
beginner.body: Mikolov names Bengio's fixed input window as a limitation and combines the current word with the previous recurrent state before producing a normalized next-word distribution.

beginner.heading: Separate model state from test-time learning
beginner.body: The recurrent state updates on every token. Dynamic adaptation is a different mechanism that changes model parameters during evaluation.

beginner.heading: Name every result component
beginner.body: Reported gains can involve one recurrent model, model ensembles, count-model interpolation, or online adaptation. The page keeps those configurations explicit.

beginner.heading: Recurrence does not guarantee long usable context
beginner.body: The conclusion says truly long context was not captured. The main experiments also send credit backward only one temporal step even though forward state continues recurrently.

expert.heading: Reconstruct equations 1–6
expert.body: Map the current one-hot word and previous state into x(t), update the sigmoid state s(t), and normalize y(t) over the next-word vocabulary. Preserve the paper's concatenation prose despite equation 1's printed plus sign.

expert.heading: Show forward recurrence and depth-one credit together
expert.body: The state recurrence can carry earlier activation while the reported training procedure propagates only current-step error. Neither row is evidence for the other.

expert.heading: Keep rare-word and adaptation rules explicit
expert.body: Equation 7 allocates probability inside the rare-word class, while dynamic adaptation applies test-time stochastic-gradient updates. Both are outside the recurrent-memory fixture.

expert.heading: Audit every mixture and dataset boundary
expert.body: Keep WSJ scale, ensemble, cross-data, and RT05 rows separate, including off-table perplexity 112 and the 16.3 value followed by footnote 4. No interactive control spans them.

contribution.text: Join a composite input/output/forget/peephole cell to normalized word prediction while keeping count-model interpolation visible.

beginner.heading: Assemble a later composite cell
beginner.body: The 2012 model combines the original protected cell and input/output gates with the later forget gate and later state-to-gate links. That composite must not be projected backward into 1997.

beginner.heading: Turn gated state into next-word probability
beginner.body: The paper contrasts fixed-order histories with a recurrent route, then maps a one-hot word input through recurrent memory to a normalized next-word softmax under a cross-entropy objective.

beginner.heading: Longer available context is not always better
beginner.body: The tested LSTM improves on the matched sigmoid recurrent baseline, but concatenating more sentences eventually worsens perplexity and output grouping trades quality against speed.

beginner.heading: The recognition result is a mixture result
beginner.body: The French speech-recognition system interpolates the LSTM model with a much larger Kneser–Ney model. The 0.5- and 0.3-point changes are not standalone neural-model scores.

expert.heading: Assign each visible mechanism to its source
expert.body: The target collectively cites the two later modifications. Cross-source comparison resolves adaptive forgetting to reference 12 and weighted state-to-gate links to reference 13 without claiming equation-level identity.

expert.heading: Reconstruct the word objective, not an omitted cell equation
expert.body: The paper specifies one-hot word input, softmax cross-entropy, optional projection, and class-factored output. Its cell section omits extensive equations, so a compact modern vector cell remains labelled reconstruction.

expert.heading: Preserve graph-only and corpus uncertainty
expert.body: Keep Penn Treebank and French splits, matched-parameter recurrent comparisons, projection, long-context, and output-clustering findings tied to their plotted or tabulated evidence.

expert.heading: Separate LSTM, Kneser–Ney, and interpolation
expert.body: The 1,000-best French setup combines a 27-million-word LSTM with a Kneser–Ney model trained on more than four billion words. Both WER rows remain static and component-labelled.

expert.heading: The four-page paper is not a run package
expert.body: Core comparisons are graph-only and lack uncertainty; the article omits optimizer, unrolling depth, seeds, and other settings needed for exact reconstruction. The conclusion remains correspondingly narrow.

interludes.title: What the recurrent word model changes

beginner.heading: Static word rows inside a fixed window
beginner.body: Bengio's evaluated model looks up one learned row for each of the previous n−1 word types, concatenates those rows, and uses a feed-forward network plus softmax. The rows do not change with token history, and the model is not recurrent.

beginner.heading: Recurrence remains future work
beginner.body: The framework permits recurrent implementations, but the main experiments use the finite feed-forward window. This panel supplies normalized neural word probability, not carried state.

expert.heading: Audit C, x, H, U, W, and y
expert.body: C supplies static word-feature rows; x concatenates n−1 rows; y = b + Wx + U tanh(d + Hx) supplies vocabulary scores before softmax. The direct path is optional and recurrence is absent from the evaluated form.

expert.heading: Do not transfer Elman's recurrence through the citation
expert.body: Bengio cites learned distributed symbolic representations while keeping one static row per word and a fixed window. Recurrent and paragraph-level contexts remain proposed extensions.

interludes.title: The count model remains in the reported system

beginner.heading: Return to Kneser–Ney before reading the WER row
beginner.body: The completed smoothing journey explains the count model in the French recognition mixture. Sundermeyer's paper combines that model with the LSTM score; it does not report the recognition change as a replacement of smoothing.

expert.heading: Keep component scale and interpolation explicit
expert.body: The French setup interpolates a 300-cell LSTM trained on 27 million in-domain words with a Kneser–Ney model trained on more than four billion words, then rescoring 1,000-best hypotheses. No synthetic control links their weights or corpora.
